We are seeking a reliable and safety-conscious Goods transportation Driver to join our 40 plus  team. The successful candidate will be responsible for transporting goods, or materials in a timely and professional manner while ensuring compliance with all traffic laws and company policies.

Key Responsibilities

• Safely operate company vehicles on assigned routes.
• Transport passengers or deliveries efficiently and on schedule.
• Conduct daily vehicle inspections and report maintenance issues.
• Keep accurate records of trips, mileage, and deliveries.

Qualifications

What We Offer

How to Apply

Phone: +45 53389878

**Your impact begins here

**As Senior Clinical Genetics Data Scientist, you will turn human genetic evidence into clear recommendations that guide clinical development decisions. You will lead defined projects that combine trial and population genetic data with clinical outcomes and molecular measurements. Your work will help explain disease biology, understand why people respond differently to treatment and identify where patient stratification, or asset differentiation could matter. It helps teams decide with confidence, for people living with serious chronic diseases.

**What You’ll Bring

**You are an independent, systematic scientist with sound judgement, who communicates uncertainty openly, acts on feedback and sees work through to its outcome.

• A PhD in statistical genetics, genetic epidemiology, bioinformatics or a related quantitative discipline; or a relevant master’s degree with equivalent demonstrated research and applied experience.

• Demonstrated independent ownership of complex human genetics projects, from study design and data preparation to robust interpretation and communication of results.

• Strong, hands-on experience in GWAS design, execution and interpretation, including linkage disequilibrium, population structure, relatedness, multiple testing, power and validation.

• Proficiency in R and/or Python, Linux and genetics tools such as PLINK, BCFtools, GATK, REGENIE, SAIGE or equivalent, with reproducible programming, version control, documentation and quality review.

• Practical experience processing SNP array and WGS data, including quality control, genotype harmonisation, phasing and imputation, variant calling, filtering and functional annotation.

• Hands-on experience conducting and interpreting pQTL analyses, including cis and trans mapping, multiple-testing control and integration with GWAS or colocalisation evidence.

• The ability to coordinate stakeholders, manage project risks and dependencies, and present complex findings clearly in English to audiences with different technical backgrounds.

**Desirable, But Not Essential

**Experience in clinical trial genetics, pharmacogenetics or clinical development, particularly in cardiometabolic, obesity or renal disease; rare-variant and gene-based tests, genetic risk prediction or advanced causal inference; or work with secure cloud computing, biobank-scale resources and regulated analytical environments.

**What You’ll Do

**You will own project outcomes from the scientific question to validated results and practical recommendations.

• Plan and run GWAS, pQTL and related analyses of disease phenotypes, clinical endpoints, biomarkers and treatment response, using trial and external cohort data.

• Prepare SNP array and whole-genome sequencing data into analysis-ready datasets, and use fine-mapping, colocalisation and causal inference to prioritise plausible variants, genes, pathways and biomarkers.

• Investigate pharmacogenetic associations and genetically informed subgroups, separating prognostic signals from evidence of differential treatment benefit.

• Turn findings into decision-focused reports and presentations, with clear uncertainty and limitations, and contribute genetics content to publications and regulatory documents.

• Build documented, version-controlled workflows, mentor colleagues through code review and feedback, and use genetic and clinical data within approved consent, governance and quality requirements.

**Who You’ll Work With

**You will join Clinical Omics Sciences, part of Translational & Clinical Omics in Research & Development. Here, colleagues explore scientific ideas and advance them towards clinical testing, bringing together curiosity, data, technology and collaboration.

Your closest partners will be Clinical Development Teams, translational scientists, human genetics researchers, biostatisticians, data managers and data engineers. You will also coordinate agreed work with external collaborators and suppliers. You will explain your technical choices in accessible language, build alignment on the question, deliverables and decision, and speak up early when something stalls.

**What You Can Expect Here

**You will be trusted to determine and execute the analytical approach for your projects, within agreed objectives and quality requirements. You will be supported to perform at your best, make your voice heard and grow through practical project experience, scientific feedback and relevant learning offerings. You will also help raise the standard for the whole team by shaping shared workflows, templates and methods.

Salary: For this role, the Annual Base Salary ranges from 651,000 to

956,900 DKK, corresponding to the level of the position. The placement within the salary range will be assessed during the recruitment process based on the candidate's skills, competencies, knowledge and relevant experience.

Incentives and Benefits: The salary package may include short-term and/or long-term incentives as well as other employee benefits based on position level, location, functional area and relevant market benchmarks.

Learn more about our Reward Philosophy here

**Start now

**Your impact begins today. Please apply by 27 November 2026. We review applications on an ongoing basis, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

We are an equal opportunities employer and are committed to an inclusive recruitment process and equality of opportunity for all applicants.

We seek an experienced, highly motivated, and independent laboratory technician to support the Novo Nordisk Foundation Center for Protein Design (CPD) at the University of Copenhagen (UCPH). This is a full-time position, starting as soon as possible, and employment through 31 July 2032.

  Our research:

  The CPD is a multidisciplinary centre that works across the university—notably with the Departments of Biology, Drug Design and Pharmacology, Chemistry, and Computer Science—and with national and international academic and industrial partners. CPD is funded by an initial grant of 700M DKK for seven years from the Novo Nordisk Foundation. At capacity, the CPD is expected to have ≈8 research groups, ≈80 researchers, and support staff. Research will encompass the growing protein design landscape with computational, experimental, applied and hybrid projects.

  The CPD's vision and mission are to accelerate protein design by deepening understanding of sequence-to-structure/function relationships in proteins, and to train the next generation of protein scientists to apply protein-design approaches and methods to a diverse array of fundamental and real-world challenges.  

  CPD research is broadly organised into three themes: Programmable De Novo Protein Design, aimed at improving methods for protein design by combining rational, physics-based and AI-based approaches; Contextualised Protein Design, which is about designing proteins that are fit for purpose, such as working directly and optimally in cells, chemical reactors, etc.; and Biodesign for Sustainability and Healthcare, for instance working with biotech and industry to deliver synthetic proteins to address grand challenges in these areas.

  Further information on the CPD see: cpd.ku.dk.

  Your job:

  Specifically, we seek a talented laboratory technician and team player to help set up, equip and support research in newly refurbished labs. You will join the CPD Operations and Management Team, work closely with another laboratory technician and the CPD Experimental Officer, and fulfil a key role supporting CPD researchers.

  Tasks of the Laboratory Technician will include:

   	
• Assist in setting up, establishing, and organising newly refurbished CPD laboratories together with a laboratory technician and the CPD Experimental Officer. 	
• Order, track, and manage laboratory supplies, consumables, and chemical inventory, including invoice processing. 	
• Solicit and evaluate quotes from multiple vendors for large equipment purchases in accordance with university and public procurement guidelines. 	
• Process purchase orders, verify deliveries, monitor invoices, and register new equipment. 	
• Serve as a key contributor to safety compliance, chemical registration, and risk assessment coordination. 	
• Drive and maintain environmental sustainability initiatives in KU, targeting LEAF (Laboratory Efficiency Assessment Framework) 	
• Establish and maintain rigorous safety routines, waste management and documentation. 	
• Contribute to onboarding new researchers, visiting scientists, and students, including safety introductions, lab space allocation, and workflow introductions. 	
• Contribute to the offboarding processes by ensuring proper handover of samples and data and chemical/waste disposal. 	
• Prepare shared stock solutions and reagents 	
• Contribute to practical laboratory classes and guide new researchers on standard operating procedures.   Profile:

  To succeed in this role, we anticipate that you have a lab technician (laborant) degree or similar. We also expect you to be a service-minded team player who likes managing the day-to-day operation of a laboratory, including carrying out administrative tasks like obtaining quotations and handling purchasing and procurement activities.

  Preferably, you have experience with hands-on expertise in solid-phase peptide synthesis and peptide purification, solid knowledge of biochemistry laboratory safety regulations, and a keen interest in collaborating with researchers from different backgrounds. You should bring a strong motivation for optimising lab organisation and safety, alongside a genuine interest in teaching students and guiding new researchers within a dynamic, international academic environment.

  Essential experience and skills

   	
• Highly structured, detail-oriented, and able to prioritise and execute tasks independently 	
• Knowledge of biochemical and/or chemical research and teaching laboratories 	
• Understanding of Good Laboratory Practice, chemical and biological safety regulations, standard documentation practices, and inventory management 	
• Strong and proven organisational, communication, and networking skills 	
• Good written and spoken Danish and English language skills   Desirable experience and skills

   	
• Experience with solid-phase peptide synthesis (SPPS) and peptide purification 	
• Experience with Kemibrug, SDI and RejsUd 	
• Experience with the LEAF or similar green laboratory sustainability programmes 	
• Perform routine recombinant protein expression and purification to generate shared stocks 	
• Experience with mammalian cell lines and preparing bacterial competent cells   Place of employment

  The place of employment is at the NNF Center for Protein Design, located at the Department of Drug Design and Pharmacology, University of Copenhagen. We offer creative, stimulating working conditions in a dynamic, international research environment.

  Terms of salary and employment
 The employment as a laboratory technician (TAP) is a full-time (37 hours/week) position with employment through 31 July 2032. The starting date is as soon as possible, and, ideally, the successful candidate will be in place by March 2027 to coincide with the preparations for opening newly refurbished labs.

  Employment will be in accordance with the provisions of the collective agreement between the Danish Ministry of Finance and HK Stat, Organisationsaftalen for kontorfunktionærer, laboranter og it-medarbejdere. You can read more about salary levels in the state sector on this page Lønoverblik

  The monthly salary will be based on of work experience, with the possibility to negotiate a salary supplement based on prior experience and qualifications.

  Questions
 For further information regarding the position, please contact CPD Experimental Officer, Ana Almeida, ana.almeida@sund.ku.dk.

  Learn more about the Department of Drug Design and Pharmacology, https://drug.ku.dk/, and Center for Protein Design https://cpd.ku.dk/

  Application
 Your application should be in English and include:

   	
• A cover letter outlining your fit to the role and motivation for applying (max. one page) 	
• Curriculum Vitae (incl. the names of two references (max. two pages)  	
• A certified/signed copy of certificate(s) of education   Please submit your application by clicking on “Apply Now” below. Only online applications will be accepted.

  Application deadline: 4 January 2027, 23:59 [CET]

  We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications that do not meet the above requirements.

  Interviews are expected to be held in January 2027.

  The University of Copenhagen wishes to reflect the diversity of society and welcomes applications from all qualified candidates, regardless of age, disability, gender, nationality, race, religion, or sexual orientation. Appointment will be based on merit alone.

  As part of the International Alliance of Research Universities (IARU) and among Europe’s top-ranking universities, the University of Copenhagen promotes research and teaching to the highest international standard. Rich in tradition and modern in outlook, the University gives students and staff the opportunity to cultivate their talent in an ambitious and informal environment. An effective organisation – with good working conditions and a collaborative work culture – creates the ideal framework for a successful academic career.

jobs.description:
At ABB, we help industries run leaner and cleaner—and every person here makes that happen. You’ll be empowered to lead, supported to grow, and proud of the impact we create together. Join us and help run what runs the world.

**This position reports to:

**Engineering Manager

__

**Your Role And Responsibilities

**Do you have extensive experience with System 800xA and a strong background in troubleshooting complex process plants? Are you ready to take on a key specialist role where you define automation architecture and develop advanced technical solutions for our customers?

If so, this is your opportunity to make a significant technical impact within ABB’s Life Science business.

ABB delivers large-scale 800xA systems to leading Pharma and Life Science customers in Denmark. The success of these projects is driving a growing pipeline, and you will play a central role in shaping future opportunities. As a technical lead, you will contribute to development projects and work closely with our business development team on upcoming initiatives.

In this role, you will collaborate with ABB engineers, project managers, and service account managers across multiple customer projects in Life Science production environments. As a System 800xA specialist, you will take ownership of complex troubleshooting, guide architectural decisions, and identify optimal solutions.

With your deep expertise in System 800xA, automation architecture, and process control libraries, you will solve high-complexity challenges that others cannot – both for customers and their sub-suppliers.

You can be based in Ballerup, Kalundborg, or Middelfart. However, you should expect to be on-site with customers in Bagsværd and/or Kalundborg at least one day per week, with increased presence during critical project phases.

**Your Responsibilities

**

• Coordination with relevant internal ABB functions for resolution of complex technical issues for customers.

• Diagnose and troubleshoot on technical issues - evaluation of problem descriptions, analysis of log files, remote diagnostics in installed base, etc.

• Take the lead in maturing and developing architecture for new projects.

• Consult the customer with the right solutions based on technical knowledge and support from ABB organization.

• Develop, test, document and PoC in technical solutions and support your colleagues in executing.

**Qualifications For The Role

**

• Minimum 5 years of hands-on experience in 800xA with AC800M process in larger size process automation projects.

• In depth experience with 800xA system and control libraries (e.g. PCDL, PCEL) from troubleshooting and development

• Solid experience with test, commissioning, and hypercare phases of an automation project, and familiar with typical issues raised during these phases.

• Experience from ABB R&D organization is an advantage.

• Experience within Life Science industries and batch management is an advantage.

• Ability to understand customer requirements and challenges with a service-minded approach.

• Experience in working either within or together with the L3 support team or L4 R&D.

• Demonstrating ownership, applying a problem-solving solution-oriented mindset and strong communication skills.

**More About Us

**At ABB, we have a clear goal of promoting diversity and inclusion in terms of gender, LGBTQ+, disability, ethnicity, and age. Together, we have embarked on a journey where we all individually and collectively celebrate and welcome individual differences. You can look forward to joining an organization with very good well-being. Collaboration and team spirit are key words for us and a crucial foundation for reaching our shared goals. We prioritize a good working environment highly and continuously invest in the education and development of you and your colleagues. If you want to read more about our continuous work with the working environment and sustainability, you can find more information at: https://global.abb/group/en/sustainability.

When you join ABB, you become part of a global, world-leading technology company known for innovation, quality, and opportunity. In ABB’s Life Science organization, you will be part of a highly successful business with a strong brand, a clear strategy, and an exciting project pipeline for the coming years. Equally important, you will enjoy a positive work environment characterized by respect, helpfulness, and a supportive tone.

You will be part of our Life Science Engineering team, collaborating with experienced engineers. We are an international group of approx. 50 project engineers in Denmark. In addition, we collaborate with +50 colleagues from the global ABB organization.

You will have a fixed base in our office in Ballerup, Kalundborg or Middelfart, where most of your close colleagues are also based. We also offer the possibility of working from home a few days a week.

The position reports to Engineering Manager, Lars Schultz.

Apply for the job online via our simple and easily accessible system, where you can also save selected jobs. If you have questions about the position before then, you are welcome to contact Lars Schultz at +45 2497 8635. You can also find more information about us on our website www.abb.com.

The application deadline is 08.12.2026. We look forward to receiving your application.

_ABB is a global technology leader in electrification and automation, enabling a more sustainable future with efficient use of resources. By connecting our knowledge in engineering and digitalization, ABB makes industry more efficient, productive, sustainable and able to improve their performance. At ABB, we call it 'Engineered to Outrun'. The company has over 140 years of history and more than 105,000 employees worldwide. In Denmark, you will have more than 500 colleagues in offices in Ballerup, Middelfart, Esbjerg, Kalundborg and Aalborg.

__Join us. Be part of the team where progress takes place, industries transform, and your work shapes the world.

Run What Runs the World.

__#RunWithABB

_Building a cleaner, smarter future takes all kinds of minds: the curious, the courageous, and the creative. That's why we welcome people from all backgrounds and experiences.

Ready to make an impact?

Apply today or visit https://www.abb.com to learn more about the impact of our solutions across the globe.

At Factbird, we're redefining how manufacturing runs. By combining hardware, firmware, cloud, and AI, we turn raw production data into real, measurable impact on factory floors around the world. This is a product built by and for people who understand what happens on the shop floor. We’re on a mission to make it easier and faster for manufacturers to work smarter to increase productivity and eliminate waste.

For this mission we're building fast, scaling with purpose, and solving problems that matter. Now, we're looking for an addition to our product management team, who want to bring our product into the future by expanding upon how we create real value on the factory floor.

The position product management plays at Factbird is both high-impact and also hands-on. As a product manager here, you’ll set direction, own the roadmap, and drive execution from idea to launch and beyond. You’ll play a key role in shaping how our platform scales and how our customers succeed.

About the role

You’ll work closely with a dedicated development team and your peer product leaders, and you report to the Director of Product.

Production Insights: As a key platform application the candidate requires a strong PM backbone with a focus on having built products that communicate complex datasets and provide actionable insights to different user groups. To succeed in this role, previous experience from manufacturing industries is a key differentiator for us. Whether you have stood on that shopfloor and owned its numbers yourself or have worked for manufacturing and know exactly what "real value" means to the people running a production line – we take “knowing our customers” very serious for this particular position.

Key Responsibilities

• Turn strategy into shipped products: Define roadmaps, prioritize ruthlessly, and work closely with stakeholders to ensure we solve the biggest problems our customers are facing.

• Lead across disciplines: Act as the glue between product, firmware, cloud, UX, and business stakeholders - making sure everyone is aligned, focused, and moving fast.

• Identify signals in noise: Clarify customer needs, outline their jobs to be done and translate findings into clear and concise user stories.

• Spearhead continuous discovery: Build and maintain strong relationships with both internal and external stakeholders to gather key insights.

• Launch, learn, iterate: Drive product launches, gather customer feedback, and continuously evolve features based on real-world usage.

• Own performance & outcomes: Define and track key performance metrics aligned with product objectives.

About you

You have experienced first-hand how a shop floor is operated to ensure targets are met and continuous improvements are realized. You thrive in environments where ownership is high, pace is fast, and impact is visible. You're comfortable making decisions with imperfect information and love turning complexity into clarity, because you've had to do exactly that on a production floor before.

You are curious about technology and are keen to figure out what it enables for people who live and breathe shop floor realities every day. You care deeply about understanding the underlying problem before working on a solution. You want to build products that drive real value, something customers depend on, not just move on to the next shiny thing.

Requirements

• Solid Product Management Experience: You are well-versed in product management frameworks and agile processes and can bring them into play with a practical approach, leveraging frameworks where they create clarity, structure, and speed.

• You've worked hands-on on the shopfloor for a while. You've been accountable for ensuring performance meets expectations by collaborating with the likes of operators, process engineers, continuous improvement leads, and plant or operations managers. This operational depth is what lets you translate real production pain into product decisions, and it is a hard requirement for this specific role — without it, the rest of the role is very difficult to do well. Our products play an essential role in manufacturing operations, and your experience within this field is essential.

• A continuous discovery mindset: You talk to customers constantly, map their jobs to be done, and identify commonalities. You're comfortable sitting with ambiguity until the real problem surfaces.

• Strong data and analytics instinct: Comfortable working with data and understanding how to turn analysis into concrete actions.

• A natural communicator: You speak the language of engineers, designers, operators, and leadership alike, adapting how you communicate to whoever's in the room.

• Driving teams: Proven ability to set and agree direction and goals with R&D teams, driving the team and getting to results in a manner where the team feels proud of the outcome.

Why Factbird?

People are at the heart of everything we build. We believe great products come from empowered teams — and we work hard to create an environment where you can do your best work and have space for life beyond it.

Here's what you can look forward to:

• Flexible working hours: We trust you to manage your time. Life isn’t one-size-fits-all, and neither is work.

• Competitive salary: We offer compensation that reflects your skills, experience, and impact.

• Internet reimbursement: Stay connected and productive, wherever you choose to work from.

• Thoughtful, human onboarding: We’ll support you step by step, giving you the context, tools, and guidance you need to feel confident from day one.

• A career path that grows with you: Through bi-yearly Individual Development Plan conversations, we’ll work together to shape a career journey that fits your ambitions.

• Company-wide kickoffs & team days: We regularly come together across teams and regions to connect, celebrate, and align on what’s next.

• A global, inclusive culture: We’re proud of our diverse backgrounds and perspectives — and we actively celebrate them in how we work and collaborate.

We’d love to hear from you

If this role feels like a match, we’d be excited to hear from you and explore how you could help shape the future of data collection and production monitoring at Factbird.

And if someone in your network comes to mind who might be a great fit — feel free to share this opportunity with them.

Have questions? You can always reach out to Khristel, our Global Talent Acquisition & People Operations Lead at **khma@factbird.com

**_At Factbird, we believe that great work starts with people feeling respected, valued, and included. We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer and are committed to building a workplace where everyone has the opportunity to thrive.

__All employment decisions at Factbird are made based on business needs, role requirements, and individual qualifications, without discrimination based on gender, gender identity or expression, age, disability, marital or family status, nationality, ethnic or social origin, religion or belief, sexual orientation, or any other characteristic protected under applicable European and local employment laws.

_We celebrate diversity in all its forms and believe that different backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences make our teams stronger and our work better. We warmly encourage all qualified candidates to apply and to bring their whole selves to Factbird.

At BlinkTroll, we’re building next-generation training systems and defense technology used by military and police forces across Europe. Our mission is simple but urgent: to support the defenders of the free world with powerful, practical, and life-saving technology.

We’re looking for an Electronics Engineer to join our team in Odense, someone who can work independently, communicate clearly across disciplines, and take ownership of electronics from the first block diagram to a tested board in the field.

This role is ideal for an engineer who enjoys solving real problems, building robust hardware for tough conditions, and working closely with a small team of mechanical, software, and embedded engineers.

What You’ll Do

• Design electronics from requirements and architecture to component selection and schematics

• Create PCB layouts (Altium Designer or KiCad) with focus on signal integrity, power, thermal performance and EMC

• Build prototypes, bring up new boards and debug hardware together with embedded engineers

• Plan and carry out verification, environmental and EMC pre-compliance testing

• Prepare production files (Gerber, BOM, assembly drawings) and work with PCB and EMS partners

• Work closely with mechanical engineers on integration, board space and enclosures

• Take full ownership of design documentation, component libraries and version control

• Manage component lifecycle, obsolescence and second sources to keep products buildable

• Contribute ideas and improvements to system architecture and product design

Who You Are

• 5–10 years of hands-on experience developing electronics, from schematic to series production

• Degree in electronics, electrical engineering or a related field

• Experienced in schematic design and multilayer PCB layout in Altium Designer or KiCad

• Solid skills in analog, digital and power electronics, including microcontroller designs and common interfaces (SPI, I²C, UART, CAN, USB, Ethernet)

• Hands-on with board bring-up and debugging using oscilloscopes, logic analysers and other lab equipment

• Understanding of EMC/EMI and designing for manufacturing

• Nice to have: battery-powered or ruggedised products, RF/wireless, or defense/industrial standards (MIL-STD, IP ratings, CE marking)

• Reliable, structured, and comfortable in a fast-moving startup environment

• Based in or near Odense, or willing to work on-site

• Eligible for security clearance

What We Offer

• Work on technology with real-world impact

• A hands-on engineering environment in Odense’s robotics and defense ecosystem

• A small, ambitious team where your ideas matter

• Direct influence on product and technical direction

• Freedom to choose and improve your tools, including Altium or KiCad

• Strong team culture

• Opportunity to grow with the company

If this sounds like the right next step in your journey, we’d love to hear from you.

Let us know why you’re interested and what you’d bring to the role, please submit your application through our website

Join Teradyne Robotics and help redefine automation. Shape next year’s innovations. Move a fast-growing industry forward. Build a career that matters. You can do it all here. jobs.occupation: PhD position in biogas production from hydrothermal liquefaction process water
jobs.description:
Applicants are invited for a PhD fellowship/scholarship at Graduate School of Technical Sciences, Aarhus University, Denmark, within the Biological and Chemical Engineering programme. The position is available from 1 April 2027 or later. You can submit your application via the link under 'how to apply'.

Title:
PhD position in biogas production from hydrothermal liquefaction process water

Research area and project description:
Hydrothermal liquefaction (HTL) converts wet biogenic residues such as manure, biogas digestate and organic household waste into a renewable biocrude that can be upgraded to marine and aviation fuels. Alongside the biocrude, HTL produces large volumes of process water rich in dissolved organics and nitrogen. Treating this water efficiently while recovering its energy and nutrients is essential for the sustainability and economics of future full-scale HTL plants.

The PhD position is part of the Horizon Europe Innovation Action CARAVEL (2027-2030), coordinated by Aarhus University with 16 partners from 8 countries. CARAVEL will demonstrate the first integrated HTL value chain at TRL8, including circular management of process water and hydrochar. It is a collaborative project, so frequent exchange with the international partners from academia and industry is essential.

The PhD project will investigate anaerobic digestion (AD) as a route to convert HTL process water into biogas while managing nitrogen. HTL process water contains compounds such as phenols and N-heterocycles that can inhibit methanogenesis, and inhibition thresholds depend on feedstock and process conditions. The PhD student will determine biomethane potential and inhibitory effects of process waters from different feedstocks in batch co-digestion tests with manure, demonstrate co-digestion in a full-scale experimental thermophilic biogas reactor, and optimise mono-digestion in a pilot-scale anaerobic fixed-bed biofilter, including micro-aeration to enhance the degradation of inhibitory compounds. A central aim is to link process water composition to methane yield, process stability and nitrogen conversion.

The work combines laboratory experiments with pilot- and full-scale operation at AU Foulum, which hosts both HTL and biogas research facilities. Techniques include biomethane potential testing, reactor operation, gas analysis, VFA, COD and nitrogen analysis, and GC-MS characterisation of process water.

Qualifications and specific competences:
Applicants must have a relevant Master's degree, e.g. in environmental, chemical or biological engineering, biotechnology, microbiology or a similar field.

Experience with anaerobic digestion, biogas processes or wastewater treatment is expected. Practical experience with laboratory or pilot-scale bioreactor operation and relevant analytical techniques (e.g. gas chromatography, VFA, COD and nitrogen analysis) is desired. Knowledge of hydrothermal liquefaction or other thermochemical conversion technologies is an advantage but not a requirement.

The successful candidate has demonstrated excellent academic results, has good collaboration and communication skills in English and is also able to work independently.

Place of employment and place of work:
The place of employment is Aarhus University, and the place of work is Burrehøjvej 43, 8830 Tjele, Denmark.

Contacts:
Applicants seeking further information regarding the PhD position are invited to contact:
 
• Professor Henrik Bjarne Møller, e-mail: henrikb.moller@bce.au.dk (main supervisor)
• Associate Professor Patrick Biller, e-mail: pbiller@bce.au.dk (co-supervisor)
 For information about application requirements and mandatory attachments, please see our application guide. If answers cannot be found there, please contact:

For technical reasons, you must upload a project description. Please copy the project description above and upload it as a PDF in the application.

Please note:

• The programme committee may request further information or invite the applicant to attend an interview.
• Shortlisting will be used, which means that the evaluation committee only will evaluate the most relevant applications.
 Formalities and salary range
Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions. You will be employed as an academic staff member at basic salary grades 4–8. As a PhD fellow you will also receive a monthly non-pensionable allowance.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

jobs.occupation: Postdoc in Mechatronic Design for Remotely Operated Vehicles
jobs.description:
Centre for Industrial Mechanics (CIM), part of the Institute of Mechanical and Electrical Engineering, University of Southern Denmark (SDU), invites application for an 18-month postdoc position within Mechatronic Design for Remotely Operated Vehicles (ROVs). The position is available from March 2027, and the specific start date will be agreed upon with the successful candidates.

 

What we offer 

Successful candidates will join an interdisciplinary engineering research environment at SDU Sønderborg and contribute to the development of ROVs and associated subsea mechatronics. The work combines engineering design, numerical modelling, prototyping, fabrication, integration, and experimental validation in laboratory and marine environments.

The positions offer opportunities to:

• 
Develop and evaluate mechatronic components, subsystems, and integrated ROV platforms.

• 
Design underwater actuation mechanisms, transmissions, structural components, and pressure-resistant enclosures, including sealing and mechanical interfaces.

• 
Integrate underwater sensors, actuators, embedded electronics, and control hardware.

• 
Perform CAD modelling, engineering analysis, simulations, design optimisation, and prototype fabrication.

• 
Conduct laboratory and field testing to improve the performance, reliability, and robustness of subsea mechatronic technologies.

• 
Publish research in international scientific journals and conferences, collaborate with research partners, and contribute to student supervision where relevant.

 

What we expect 

Applicants must hold a PhD degree in mechatronics, mechanical engineering, robotics, marine engineering, or a closely related discipline at the time of employment. We seek motivated researchers with strong mechatronic design skills and hands-on experience in developing, integrating, and testing electromechanical systems.

Applicants should have demonstrated expertise in mechatronic design and practical experience in several of the following areas:

• 
Mechanical and mechatronic design, including actuation, transmissions, structural design, and electromechanical integration.

• 
CAD and engineering modelling or analysis, such as finite element analysis, multibody dynamics, or related methods.

• 
Integration of sensors, actuators, embedded electronics, and control hardware.

• 
Rapid prototyping, additive manufacturing, machining, assembly, and experimental development.

• 
Experimental testing, instrumentation, data acquisition, system characterisation, and troubleshooting.

• 
Basic programming and control using tools such as Python, C/C++, MATLAB/Simulink, or ROS/ROS 2.

Experience in subsea engineering, ROV development, underwater actuation, pressure-resistant enclosures, waterproofing, sealing, or marine instrumentation is an advantage but not a requirement. Applicants should have a publication record appropriate to their career stage, sound scientific judgement, good written and spoken English, and the ability to work both independently and collaboratively.

 

Workplace description 

The positions will be based at the Centre for Industrial Mechanics (CIM), Department of Mechanical and Electrical Engineering, Faculty of Engineering, University of Southern Denmark, in Sønderborg. The research environment brings together expertise in mechanical engineering, mechatronics, modelling, control, and experimental engineering.

Get a glimpse of (work)life through the eyes of some of our many excellent researchers at SDU in Sønderborg. 

 

Further information

• 
Mrudul Chellapurath, Assistant Professor, at mrch@sdu.dk

• 
Motivated application.

• 
Curriculum Vitae. 

• 
Master’s and PhD degree certificates or equivalent (original and an official English translation).  

• 
Complete list of publications highlighting the publications most relevant to the position.

• 
A research statement.

•

• 
Documentation of other qualifications relevant to the position may also be included.

All documents must be in English and PDF format. CPR number (civil registration number) must be crossed out. All PDF-files must be unlocked, allow binding and may not be password protected. 

SUBMISSION GUIDE: Motivated application must be uploaded under ‘Cover letter’ (max. 5 MB), Curriculum Vitae must be uploaded under ‘Resume’ (max 5 MB). All other documents must be uploaded under ‘Miscellaneous documents’ (max 10 files with a maximum 50 MB per file). 

 

The application deadline is December 10, 2026, at 11:59 PM/23:59 (CET/CEST) 

 

Assessment and selection process

Applications will be assessed by an expert or assessment committee. Shortlisting may be applied, and only shortlisted candidates will receive a written assessment. Read about shortlisting at SDU. Interviews and tests may be part of the overall evaluation. Read about the Assessment and selection process.  

 

Employment terms

Appointment as a postdoc is temporary for an initial 18-month period, and the preferred start date is from March 2027. Extension may be possible depending on available funding. 

Employment as a postdoc requires academic qualifications at PhD level at the time of employment. Employment will be in accordance with the collective agreement between the Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations for academics in the state including the associated circular on the protocol for the job structure for academic staff at Danish universities and the provisions for postdoc as described therein. 

Salary is determined in accordance with the applicable collective agreement and based on objective and gender-neutral criteria, including the content of the position, responsibilities, and qualification requirements. SDU Centre for Industrial Software in Sønderborg, part of the Software Engineering units at SDU situated at the Maersk Mc-Kinney Moller Institute, University of Southern Denmark (SDU), invites applications for one or more positions within AI Engineering. The positions are open from beginning of 2027, and the specific start date will be agreed with the successful candidates. 

The application deadline is December 7, 2026, at 11.59 PM/23.59 (CET).

 

What we offer

With a position at SDU, you will:

• 
be part of one of our dynamic research centres with both a national and international profile, while working in areas of tremendous potential and societal relevance;

• 
join collaborations across the university, as well as with national, international, and industrial research partners;

• 
help establish joint innovation projects in close collaboration with industry and the local society;

• 
help build up the research and educational environment;

• 
contribute to the teaching programmes in Software Engineering at the highest level for undergraduate and graduate students at SDU;

• 
join a harmonious workplace environment that is conducive to productivity, promotes creativity, and rewards and recognizes individuals and group achievement;

• 
have the opportunity to live and work in one of the happiest countries in the world that also offers excellent and free health and education systems.

 

What we expect

The focus of the SDU Centre for Industrial Software is research and education in software engineering, embedded systems, cyber-security and AI engineering. We see these areas complementing each other to make way for the engineering of the next generation of reliable, intelligent and embedded software solutions. We are particularly interested in software operated in real life, systems that adapt at runtime, span embedded devices, edge infrastructure and the cloud, that people work with and trust, and that increasingly answer to regulation. This includes understanding how new technologies change the engineering of products and software infrastructures.

The positions are open in any of the AI engineering research areas of interest to the centres, which include:

• 
AI Engineering (e.g. multi-modal machine learning)

• 
AI integration in mobile, wearable and embedded platforms

• 
Human-AI collaboration in the context of mobile, wearable and embedded platforms

• 
Domain-oriented AI Engineering (e.g., medical, energy or manufacturing).

 

Who we are looking for

We expect applicants to hold a PhD in artificial intelligence, software engineering, computer science or a closely related discipline. For associate professors we expect a research and teaching record corresponding to several years of independent work after the PhD, including documented teaching and supervision experience.

We are looking for candidates who have demonstrated research excellence appropriate to their career stage, who show a clear path towards an independent and internationally recognised research programme, and who are able and willing to contribute to competitive national and international funding applications. We also expect an interest in working across disciplines, in supervising students and junior researchers, and in teaching and advising in software engineering at all levels.

We particularly welcome applications from candidates who publish in leading venues in the field. If your work is more domain oriented and you therefore publish in leading venues within a specific domain, you are also very welcome to apply.

Fluency in English is required. Knowledge of Danish is not a requirement, and successful applicants will be offered Danish language courses.

 

Workplace description

The University of Southern Denmark

The University of Southern Denmark is one of the youngest universities in Denmark, founded in 1966. The university is founded around the goal of providing the right knowledge at the right time to support society. The university targets major, complex societal problems of a cross-disciplinary nature such as climate, welfare, health and technology, tackling these in collaboration across faculties.

The Faculty of Engineering

The Faculty of Engineering is driven by the urge to create value for and with society, by curiosity and by the will to create that which only a few could imagine would be possible. Through research, education and collaboration, it is the ambition of the faculty to nurture talent, address challenges, create possibilities, and promote sustainable development. The faculty is strongly engaged with national and international industries and organizations over a broad range of technical domains.

The Maersk Mc-Kinney Moller Institute

The Maersk Mc-Kinney Moller Institute is an internationally recognized institute, which has maintained a leading position in robotics for more than three decades. The department is the 2nd largest department at SDU, with more than 230 staff members and 1500 students. The institute has over the last decades expanded its activities in interactive technologies, artificial intelligence, and software engineering including building several strong research centres at the SDU campuses in Odense, Sønderborg and Vejle. Thereby, the institute today covers a wide range of areas in robotics, software, AI, and applied informatics.

jobs.occupation: Vi søger en dygtig negletekniker – fuldtid og hurtigst muligt
jobs.description:
Vi søger en engageret og erfaren negletekniker på fuldtid til vores neglesalon på Amager.

Vores salon har mange faste kunder og oplever stor efterspørgsel. Derfor søger vi en dygtig negletekniker, som kan være med til at sikre den høje kvalitet og gode service, som vores kunder forventer.

Du bliver ansvarlig for at levere behandlinger af høj kvalitet og skabe flotte, kreative og personlige nailart-designs til vores kunder.

Vi søger en kreativ og fantasifuld negletekniker, der er dygtig til sit håndværk og har erfaring med forskellige behandlinger, herunder akrylnegle, gelenegle, Shellac, pedicure og avanceret nailart.

Det er et vigtigt krav, at du kan udføre et komplet nyt sæt negle på maksimalt 1 time, samtidig med at kvaliteten af arbejdet er i top.

Vi lægger stor vægt på, at du er ansvarlig, pålidelig og har lyst til at udvikle dine kompetencer sammen med vores salon. Du skal være smilende, imødekommende og serviceminded, da vi sætter stor pris på vores gode relationer til kunderne og ønsker at give dem en positiv oplevelse hver gang.

Vi forventer, at du:

-        Har solid erfaring som negletekniker.
-        Kan udføre et nyt sæt negle på maksimalt 1 time.
-        Er ekstremt dygtig til forskellige nailart-designs.
-        Har gode færdigheder inden for akrylnegle, gelenegle, Shellac og pedicure.
-        Er kreativ og har sans for detaljer og æstetik.
-        Er ansvarsbevidst, pålidelig og kvalitetsbevidst.
-        Er smilende, imødekommende og serviceminded.

Vi tilbyder:

-        En fuldtidsstilling i en etableret neglesalon på Amager.
-        Mange faste kunder og en travl hverdag.
-        Et godt, dynamisk og kollegialt arbejdsmiljø.
-        Løn efter kvalifikationer.

Er du passioneret omkring dit fag og har de nødvendige færdigheder og erfaringer? Så glæder vi os til at modtage din ansøgning og dit CV.

Vi glæder os til at høre fra dig!

We’re looking for an experienced Financial Controller to take full ownership of our numbers as we scale. You’ll run a tight month-end close, get our SaaS revenue accounting airtight, and build the finance processes that let us grow fast without drowning in manual work. If you like turning messy into robust, read on.

About Pandektes

Legal research hasn’t changed much in decades. Lawyers still spend countless hours navigating fragmented sources, outdated systems, and complex databases just to find the information they need.

At Pandektes, we’re changing that.

Our ambition is to build the leading global platform for legal research and the largest AI-powered legal database. By combining artificial intelligence, intelligent search, and continuously updated legal sources, we’re redefining how legal knowledge is accessed, understood, analyzed, and applied.

Pandektes has raised more than _€_17.5 million and most recently closed a _€_13.5 million Series A round (October 2026) led by Alstin Capital, PROfounders and Scale Capital. Pandektes already serves more than 450 customers across Denmark, Germany and Switzerland.

We’re still early in the journey, and joining our team now means you’ll have big impact on shaping how we scale.

About the role

This is a hands-on role responsible for ensuring the accuracy and integrity of financial information, overseeing the month-end close, management accounts, financial reporting and statutory compliance, while continuously improving financial processes, systems and internal controls and working closely with Senior Management, external service providers and the wider business teams. The role will combine strong technical accounting expertise with a proactive, solutions-focused approach and the ability to operate effectively in a fast-paced, evolving environment.

What you’ll do

• 
Own the monthly and annual close – reviewing journals, accruals, prepayments, provisions and balance sheet reconciliations, and delivering accurate trial balances and financial statements on time

• 
Make sure our SaaS revenue (subscription, usage-based and implementation) is recognised correctly, and reconcile revenue schedules to billing, contracts and the general ledger

• 
Produce reliable monthly P&L, balance sheet and cash flow reporting

• 
Take over revenue billing from the sales team and run it within finance

• 
Manage our outsourced service providers and review the reconciliations they prepare – bank, intercompany, payroll, fixed assets and other control accounts

• 
Design and maintain financial policies, controls and approval limits across payments, expenses, procurement and system access

• 
Oversee AP, AR and cashbook accounting, manage payments through Corepay, and keep an eye on working capital

• 
Lead statutory accounts and external audits, and oversee VAT, corporate tax and compliance with our tax advisers

• 
Coordinate intercompany accounting and reporting across our entities in Denmark, Germany, Switzerland and the UK

• 
Improve finance processes, systems and automation – and over time, build and develop a small accounting team

What you’ll bring

• 
7+ years in commercially focused accounting roles, ideally with previous experience as a Financial Controller

• 
A recognised Danish accounting qualification (or equivalent, e.g. ACA, ACCA or CIMA)

• 
Hands-on experience with subscription and deferred revenue, including month-end revenue reconciliations

• 
A track record of independently running the month-end close and producing accurate management accounts

• 
Experience with intercompany balances, foreign currencies and reporting across international subsidiaries

• 
Exposure to international tax, VAT and transfer pricing, and experience running a local audit process

• 
A strong grasp of internal controls, segregation of duties and fraud risk

• 
Experience improving finance operations in a growing, scaling business – and a love for systems and automation

• 
A sharp eye for detail and the analytical instinct to tell a real business issue from an accounting error

How we work

We place great value on a vibrant, inspiring, and challenging company culture. This is achieved through a talented and passionate team that believes in achieving great things together.

We value curiosity and the generosity to bring other people along. If you find something useful, show us. If an experiment fails, we’d like to hear about that too.

We believe that ownership is what brings us the best teams – you can expect a lot of freedom and responsibility. The key is open communication, trust, and a shared passion to transform the legal world.

We are a growing team based in Copenhagen, Hamburg, London and Zurich. This role will be based in our Copenhagen HQ.

What we offer

• 
Competitive compensation + an attractive warrant program

• 
A collaborative work environment where your input is not only valued but often implemented within hours

• 
A central office in Copenhagen, where you can work closely with an ambitious and growing team

• 
International team events – last time we went to Barcelona, and we’d love to have you join us next time

• 
25 vacation days per year + public holidays

• 
Your own Pleo card for necessary work expenses

• 
Paid parental leave

Pandektes is an equal opportunity employer

We believe diverse teams build better products and stronger teams. We embrace and encourage people from all backgrounds to apply regardless of race/ethnicity, colour, religion, nationality, gender, sex, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, socio-economic status, culture or beliefs.

Position, purpose & impact:

We're looking for an experienced Senior People & Culture Business Partner to be the main P&C partner for our Go-To-Market organization, with a special focus on our US team. You'll be the go-to HR expert for the US, so you need solid, hands-on experience with US HR practices, benefits and systems.

Working closely with our CRO and GTM leaders, you'll strengthen performance, leadership and engagement across the business. You'll also support organizational development, talent decisions and change initiatives. You'll be based in our Copenhagen office, support US colleagues across time zones and travel to the US about every second month. Your work will help build the high-performing, trust-based culture that drives Queue-it's growth.

Your toolkit:

• 
Several years of experience as an HR Business Partner in a senior role, including organizational development and performance management.

• 
Previous hands-on HR experience supporting employees and leaders in the US.

• 
Solid knowledge of US employment practices, employee relations, benefits and HR administration.

• 
Practical experience with US HR systems and providers, such as TriNet or similar.

• 
Confidence to coach and challenge leaders while building trusted advisory relationships.

• 
Strong facilitation and communication skills across diverse stakeholder groups.

• 
Experience with stakeholder, project and change management.

• 
An analytical mindset that turns people insights into clear business recommendations.

• 
Experience supporting global organizations across cultures and time zones.

• 
Willingness to work US hours when needed and travel to the US about every second month.

The role in action:

• 
Partner with our CRO and GTM leaders on performance management, talent development and organizational effectiveness.

• 
Act as the go-to HR expert for our US organization, advising on employment practices, benefits, employee relations and HR administration.

• 
Give practical guidance on policies and compliance, and bring in external legal experts when needed.

• 
Coach and support managers through people decisions across the whole employee lifecycle.

• 
Facilitate performance dialogues, feedback processes and development conversations that lift individual and team performance.

• 
Run leadership development initiatives and employee development programs across GTM.

• 
Drive engagement initiatives and help leaders act on employee feedback, together with the wider P&C team.

• 
Support organizational changes and make sure communication and stakeholder alignment stay strong throughout.

• 
Contribute to P&C projects and strategic initiatives that support business priorities.

• 
Spend regular time with our US team, both remotely across time zones and on-site in the US.

Why join the Queue

Your Copenhagen base

Most of your time will be at our Vesterbro office in Copenhagen, Queue-it's largest office and global headquarters. The space is designed for both teamwork and focus, with open work areas, quiet rooms and dedicated spaces for deep work. You'll also spend regular time in the US, travelling there about every second month to work side by side with our US team. In between visits, you'll stay closely connected to them across time zones.

How we work

At Queue-it, you’re trusted to work in a way that suits you best, supported by a strengths-based approach and a flat hierarchy inspired by Danish work culture. You’ll be part of a global team with colleagues from 40+ nationalities, where diverse perspectives, open dialogue, and cross-cultural collaboration are part of everyday work.

Community and everyday life

We make time to connect, with regular social activities, ping pong, foosball, daily snacks, fresh fruit, great coffee, and access to a subsidized canteen in the building. It’s a workplace that balances professional growth with a strong sense of community.

What we’re about

At Queue-it, we help leading brands like Ticketmaster, Sky Mobile, and Peach Aviation navigate their busiest days with confidence. Our virtual waiting room keeps websites running smoothly during high-traffic events, creating fairer, more reliable online experiences for billions of users.

We’re also a global team of 40+ nationalities working across Denmark, the U.S., South Korea, Australia, and Japan. We believe in trust - in the digital experiences we protect and in the culture we build together.

Here, we take a strengths-based approach, encouraging people to do what they naturally do best. You’ll join a supportive environment where individuality is valued and collaboration matters.

And yes, we like to have fun. From monthly events to cultural celebrations and learning initiatives, we make time to connect, recognize one another, and enjoy the Queue.

We are empowered by trust and strengthened by people.
